## Part 1: Data Processing

# Parsing Variable Values

Write a function to GET() the URL, parse the JSON, and pull out a list of the variables with their values. (BaseR list manipulations is the easiest way to go here!)

```{r}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
obtain_url_info <- function(url) {
  
  year <- str_extract(url, "20\\d{2}")
  
  output <- GET(url)                                        #GET() the URL
  parsed <- fromJSON(rawToChar(output$content))$variables   #parse the JSON
  
  if (year %in% c("2021", "2022")) {
    parsed$STATE <- parsed$ST
  }
  
  vars <- c(                                                #pull out list of the variables
    "AGEP", "GASP", "GRPIP", "JWAP", "JWDP", "JWMNP",
    "PWGTP", "FER", "HHL", "SCH", "SCHL", "SEX",
    "STATE", "REGION", "DIVISION"
  )
  
  parsed[vars]
}
```

Obtain one list for each year

```{r}
result_21 <- obtain_url_info("https://api.census.gov/data/2021/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")
result_22 <- obtain_url_info("https://api.census.gov/data/2022/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")
result_23 <- obtain_url_info("https://api.census.gov/data/2023/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")
result_24 <- obtain_url_info("https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")
```

I saved the lists in an .rds file, and it is in my repo under the data folder

```{r}

var_desc <- list(
  yr_21 = result_21,
  yr_22 = result_22,
  yr_23 = result_23,
  yr_24 = result_24
)

saveRDS(var_desc, "data/variable_description.rds")

```

# Parsing API Data

First I get my regular URL query to work
```{r}
api <- Sys.getenv("API_KEY")

response <- GET(
  "https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1/pums",
  query = list(
    get = "AGEP,GASP,GRPIP,JWAP,JWDP,JWMNP,PWGTP",
    `for` = "state:37",
    key = api
  )
)
response
str(response)

```

This URL query will be converted into a readable format by inserting it into the helper function below
```{r}
#| warning: false
helper_response_to_tibble <- function(url_response){
  
  parsed_data <- fromJSON(rawToChar(url_response$content))
  
  column_names <- parsed_data[1, ] #first row has col names
  parsed_data <- parsed_data[-1, , drop = FALSE]
  colnames(parsed_data) <- column_names
  tibble_data <- as_tibble(parsed_data)
  
  tibble_data
}

helper_response_to_tibble(response)
```

Lets incorporate this helper into a function that accomplishes multiple goals 
```{r}
query_API <- function(year = 2024, num_vars = c("AGEP","PWGTP"), cat_vars="SEX", geo_level="State", geo_specific="37"){
  
  #if else conditions check
  
  #year = 2021, 22, 23, 24
  if (is.null(year) || !(year %in% 2021:2024)){
    stop("invalid year argument")
  }
  #PWGTP always returned + at least numeric_var (JWAP (time), JWDP (time))
  num_var_options <- c("AGEP", "GASP", "GRPIP", "JWAP", "JWDP" , "JWMNP", "PWGTP")
  
  if(!"PWGTP" %in% num_vars){
    if(length(num_vars) < 1){
      stop("need to provide a numeric argument")
    }
    num_vars <- c(num_vars, "PWGTP")
  } else if(length(num_vars) == 1){
      stop("need to provide at least one numeric argument apart from PWGTP")
  }
  
  #check if numeric var is right
  if(!num_vars %in% num_var_options){
    stop("invalid numeric argument")
  }
  
  #at least one cat_var =  FER, HHL, SCH, SCHL, and SEX
  cat_var_options <- c("FER", "HHL", "SCH", "SCHL", "SEX")
  
  if(is.null(cat_vars) || length(cat_vars)==0 ){
      stop("need to provide a categorical argument")
  }
  if(!cat_vars %in% cat_var_options){
    stop("invalid categorical argument")
  }
  
  #geo_level = state, region, division
  if(is.null(geo_level) || length(geo_level)!=1 || geo_level == "All" || !geo_level %in% c("State", "Region", "Division") ){
    stop("invalid geo level, only options are State, Region, Division")
  }
  #
  
  
  #Query URL

  
  #parse data as tibble
  
  result <- helper_response_to_tibble(response)
  class(result) <- c("census", class(result))
  
}
```
